definition: A temporary process that starts, works and exits; reusing its name later does not make a new process the same participant.
A signed entry in the daemon's append-only ledger stating that a new process continues an earlier one.
The continuing ledger account that a chain of signed succession records links processes to; every commitment, permission and checked outcome of those processes is recorded against it.
The record of checked outcomes kept against a person's account, together with any score computed from it.
The link, made by succession records, that lets a later process carry on the same person's account as an earlier one.
A job described without reference to who holds it: what must be delivered, which tools come with it, and what the holder is permitted to do.
The chain of signed succession records that links every process that has run as a person back to the first, bound to one accountable principal; written kappa in Definition 5.2.2.
A per-agent tool allowlist and scoped filesystem that bounds what an agent is technically able to do.
The live process, with a heartbeat, that holds an agent's work during one run; a respawn replaces it while the durable identity remains.

The rule that the shares a source passes to its successors sum to at most its balance, each share is debited in full from the source, and each successor receives a discounted share, so splitting or copying a record never creates credit.
A proposed record the daemon writes when it hands notes to a successor, naming the successor and the digests of the notes actually given to it.
An appended record that retracts an earlier record, such as an outcome later found invalid, while the original stays in the log.
A background rewrite of an agent's stored memory into fewer, more general entries.
Cerruti et al.'s name for memory that, with no attacker present, comes to state permissions the agent was never granted.
Zhan et al.'s name for a memory that keeps a claim while erasing the source constraints on its use.
Memory content with no pointer into the ledger, such as episodic detail or free text, which carries no authority.

Said of a consolidation that keeps every authority-bearing note pointed at and consistent with the ledger, passes every open obligation on with its full terms, counts one source once, and never rewrites a pointer-bearing note in place.
A proposed record, written by the checker, of what one consolidation changed: memory digests before and after, the consolidator and its engine, the policy version and the verdict.

Said of a score-based access mechanism in which every actor that produces a specified dishonest outcome ends up with a lower available score than its own clean continuation, counting every identity it can route work through.
Shedding a penalty by abandoning a penalized identity for a fresh one.
A reputation kept as separate scores, one per quality axis (accuracy, aesthetics, efficiency), each graded by a different kind of judge and weighted by each buyer.
In the audit-tower model, a group of auditors that one bribe can buy together; separate cliques must be bribed separately.
Audit tasks with independently established answers, designed to look like ordinary work, used to catch dishonest grading.
A cryptographic random draw whose fairness anyone can check afterwards, used here to select audits.
The settlement rule under which a caught cheat forfeits its bond but keeps the gain from cheating; the usual statement of Becker's deterrence condition assumes it.
The ordered levels of contact an agent can have with a skill in one run: listed, loaded, file read, script run.
